articleTitle: Combination of 2DPCA, sPCA, and Ridge Regression Model for Face Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICELTICs)
abstract: The 2DPCA method, an extension of the PCA method, is commonly used in pattern recognition to represent complex data in lower dimensions. One of its applications is face recognition, where it encounters the challenge of ensuring good performance in different shooting conditions while avoiding overfitting to allow for good generalizations. However, it still faces the issue of overfitting. To overcome this problem, the authors researched by combining the 2DPCA method with sPCA (sparse PCA) and the Ridge Regression Model. In this research, the 2DPCA method performs feature extraction, sPCA performs feature selection, and the Ridge Regression Model performs regularization. The results demonstrate that combining these three methods in face recognition can overcome overfitting and provide better accuracy than using the 2DPCA conventional, with an accuracy rate of 99.38%.

articleTitle: Android-Based Visualization of Vehicle Trip Data for Accident Reconstruction
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICELTICs)
abstract: Vehicle traffic accident investigations often depend on eyewitness testimony, which can be unreliable, especially in remote areas where no closed circuit television (CCTV) footage is available. A mobile data logger was developed, equipped with a range of sensors, including an accelerometer and gyroscope, to collect and store data related to vehicle movements. An additional Flutter-driven program was developed to extract and visualize data from the mobile logger, and thus improve the accuracy of accident detection and allow incidents to be rebuilt. These programs were subjected to black-box testing, which produced results consistent with the anticipated outcomes for both the recording and data visualization tests. The data visualization application was subjected to testing using the system usability scale (SUS) technique and obtained a score of 89.5, corresponding to an A grade, the highest possible score of the 5 grade levels.

articleTitle: Smart Charging Station Monitoring by Implemented SLAM Robot Arm and Challenges
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICELTICs)
abstract: Using Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) technology to build an autonomous electric vehicle charging station (AEVCS) is represents significant advancement in the fields of autonomous systems and smart infrastructures. In order to maximize the use of charging resources and improve user comfort, research article intends to design a 3D integrated charging station that can independently detect (AI) nearest vacant and travel to auto park. This paper's main goal is to combine robotic arm navigation, sensor technologies, and SLAM technology to build a charging base system that can map its surroundings in real time, locate itself, and make decisions on its own by using IOT. To properly map the charging station surroundings and identify available charging slots, the system combines LIDAR, cameras, ultrasonic sensors and central system uses the SLAM data to steer the vehicle to the designated unoccupied slot on a charging station and a robot arm for plug insertion, control room and mobile app use to improve public safety, cost efficiency and improve optimization of future charging base stations.

articleTitle: Fine-Tuning Large Language Models for Text-to-SQL Tasks in Agricultural Census Anomaly Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICELTICs)
abstract: Detecting anomalies from collected data is essential in producing high-quality data for further analysis, including agricultural census data. This research aimed to improve the efficiency of data anomaly checking by utilizing the CodeLlama- 7B Large Language Model (LLM) to translate human questions into SQL queries. Spider and WikiSQL datasets are used in the first fine-tuning phase for translating ability to general queries. The agricultural datasets are constructed using questions and queries in agricultural census database schemas and then used in the second fine-tuning phase. The LoRA method is implemented in the fine-tuning process. This fine-tuning enhanced the model's performance on the SQL-Eval framework, achieving an Average Correct Rate of 69.6%. Combining this approach with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and prompt engineering with Chain of Thought (CoT) improvedthe Average Correct Rate to 77.8%.

articleTitle: Data Analytics and Visualization in Bimanual Rehabilitation Monitoring Systems: A User-Centered Design Approach to Healthcare Professionals Decision Support
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICELTICs)
abstract: This study presents the design of a user-centered data visualization dashboard for stroke rehabilitation, which integrates the principles of visualization data analytics techniques in the field of healthcare. Addressing the complexities of visualizing for robotic bimanual rehabilitation, the design introduces novel methods to enhance data visualization, broadening monitoring capabilities, and improving the clarity of torque data. These enhancements lead to a clearer understanding of patient robot interactions. A prototype has been developed to visualize transparent torque data from a bimanual master slave robotic system, enabling healthcare professionals to monitor patient progress effectively. The dashboard features intuitive visual representations of master, slave, and assistive torques, simulating elbow joint movements through line and sunburst charts. Feedback from rehabilitation therapists during the design process ensures that the visualization approach is aligned with clinical needs. The findings suggest that the system can assist physiotherapists in devising personalized treatment strategies by providing actionable insights from the recorded data. However, additional research is needed to integrate real clinical data into the system for further enhancement and validation. This innovation has the potential to significantly improve stroke rehabilitation effectiveness and patient outcomes through a bimanual rehabilitation visualization and decision support system.

articleTitle: Modeling Bivariate Departure Delay Distribution for Estimating Slack Allocation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICELTICs)
abstract: A problem in estimating slack in airline schedule connections is investigated in this paper. We propose a method for estimating slack by analyzing historical delay data and modeling the probability distribution of primary delays. Using bivariate Kernel Density Estimation, we model the distribution as a function of time and its delay duration. Then, the distribution is used to identify flights which sensitive will be delayed. The threshold technique is applied to determine the allocated slack in flight schedule connections. As a case study, we implement the proposed method to historical departure delay data collected by an Indonesian airline. According to flight delay simulation, our proposed method works well in estimating slack since it able to reduce delay propagations.

articleTitle: Adaptive Strategies and Handover Optimization in 5G Networks to Address High Mobility Challenges
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICELTICs)
abstract: This study develops an adaptive handover strategy in 5G networks to tackle high mobility challenges and improve service continuity and quality. The research method uses a 5G network emulator with a topology of four base stations (gNBs) to test user equipment (UE) speeds of 20 km/h and 130 km/h. The adaptive algorithm developed utilizes data from the Received Signal Strength Indicator (RSSI) as well as the speed and direction of user mobility to make optimal handover decisions. The results show that at a speed of 130 km/h, the average handover latency reaches 12 ms, compared to 8 ms at 80 km/h. Additionally, the signal quality (RSSI) is lower at higher speeds, negatively affecting service quality. This adaptive algorithm successfully reduces handover latency and improves the stability and efficiency of the overall network. The testing also indicates that this adaptive algorithm can predict handover targets by considering UE speed and direction and uses hysteresis mechanisms to prevent overly frequent handovers. By employing technologies such as Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) and beamforming, this strategy is expected to maintain high service quality even under high mobility conditions.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Route Guidance Application on Android-Based Navigation System for Visually Impaired Individuals
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICELTICs)
abstract: Visually impaired or blind individuals have different needs when it comes to navigation. This research aims to design and develop an indoor navigation system for the visually impaired or blind people by utilizing Bluetooth Low Energy beacons (BLE) and Android based smartphone. BLE will provide the relative location of the user while the smartphone's Bluetooth service is on. VOSK API is integrated within this system to allow real-time speech recognition, giving the users the ability to project voice commands and receive audio feedback on current location and navigation instructions. Kalman filter is used to improve the accuracy of position tracking system. This research is limited to Building A, of Faculty Mathematics and Natural Sciences, Universitas Syiah Kuala. This research includes three main tests: accuracy testing of navigation routes using Kalman Filter and speech command recognition, functional testing and usability testing. Based on the navigation route testing using Kalman filter's Mean Squared Error (MSE), the route selection is influenced by BLE signal strength, user location, obstacles and route suggestions. A lower MSE indicates more accurate route guidance. Black box testing confirms that the developed application has passed all of the functional testing. Meanwhile, usability testing conducted using the Usability Matrix for User Experience (UMUX) obtained a score of 78.3%; which indicates that the application was well accepted by users.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of XGBoost and Random Forest for Used Car Price Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICELTICs)
abstract: Rapid technological developments have transformed the automotive industry, especially in increasing the availability and demand for used cars. Online platforms like OLX Autos are becoming increasingly popular, especially during the pandemic, as they facilitate transactions between buyers and sellers. However, pricing used cars remains a challenge. Therefore, machine learning can be one of the solutions that can be done, especially the Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) and Random Forest algorithms, to predict the price of used cars. In our works, the datasets is crawled and scraped from OLX Indonesia used car platform. The prediction evaluation results showed that the Random Forest model yielded excellent performance with hyperparameter configuration n estimators = 100, random state = 0, min samples leaf = 1, max features = 0.3, n jobs = -1, and oob score = True achieved a R-squared value of 0.9485 with a test time of 120 ms. The model is also used in used car price prediction website for different car types.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Approaches for Fire and Smoke Detection: A Comparative Study of CNN and MLP
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICELTICs)
abstract: Fire poses significant threats to buildings through-out their design lifespan, endangering human safety, causing property damage, and resulting in financial losses. Conventional fire detectors, which are predominantly sensor-based, exhibit limitations in effectively detecting fire and smoke. Consequently, computer vision-based fire detectors are emerging as a viable solution to address the shortcomings of sensor-based systems. Deep learning algorithms, including Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Multilayer Perceptrons (MLP), can be leveraged to develop such computer vision-based fire detectors, with the application of transfer learning techniques. The training and testing of these models were conducted using a dataset from Kaggle titled “Forest Fire, Smoke, Non-Fire Image Dataset.” The evaluation of the models employed metrics such as accuracy, loss, precision, recall, and F1-score. The results indicate that the CNN model exhibits better performance than MLP in accurately classifying fire and smoke images, achieving an accuracy of 98.26% compared to MLP's accuracy of 97.09%. Tuned hyperparameter values included 40 epochs, a learning rate of 1e-05, and input dimensions of (244, 244, 3). The best-performing CNN model also attained a loss of 0.0735, precision of 0.9827, recall of 0.9826, and an Fl-score of 0.9825.

articleTitle: Identification of Distribution Transformer Reliability Using the Weibull Approach at the Customer Service Unit Taman, Surabaya
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICELTICs)
abstract: The continuity of the electrical energy supply to the load is highly dependent on the electric power system's dependability. An attempt is made to maintain transformer dependability in order to guarantee appropriate distribution of electrical energy. Because of this, attempts must be made to use the Weibull distribution to assess if the transformer is in excellent condition. The MTTF value is derived from the average failure rate and serves as a reference point for the reliability rating. This is determined by the quantity of malfunctions that prevent the transformer from functioning. The results of reliability analysis using Weibull distribution on distribution transformers showed that the average failure rate was 4,72 per year, with an MTTF value of 0,23 per year, so the value The reliability obtained was 0,93. According to Croanbach's alpha, this value is classified as very reliable.

articleTitle: Sentiment Analysis Multi-Label of Toxic Comments using BERT-BiLSTM Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICELTICs)
abstract: The number of individuals accessing the Internet rises steadily each year in Indonesia. One of the reasons behind this trend is the growing popularity of online platforms like Twitter, where people can freely share their thoughts and ideas. However, it is crucial to recognize that social media can occasionally serve as a breeding ground for negative behavior, such as the spread of toxic opinions. Additionally, more information will be collected as more people become active and share their views. Therefore, a technique capable of handling this textual data comprehensively, like classification, is needed. Simple categorization methods could be more effective since they split comments into positive and negative groups. Thus, to overcome such problems, multilevel classification assigns multiple labels to a single instance, allowing its categorization into different categories inside a single statement. This research uses a combination of BERT and BiLSTM methods, whereas BERT is used to obtain word vector values and will then be used as input in the BiLSTM model to perform multi-label classification tasks. This study uses two types of word vectors, the summation of the last four hidden layers and the final hidden layer of BERT, to create a better comparison model. The study achieved an accuracy of 0.889, precision of 0.925, recall of 0.917, and an F1 score of 0.91 for the model that used the last four hidden layers of BERT as word vectors

articleTitle: Exploring Interactive Content in MOOCs for Training Educators in AI Education
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICELTICs)
abstract: The increasing demand for Artificial Intelligence (AI) skills across various sectors has required innovative teaching approaches to equip educators with the foundation of AI knowledge. Due to its dynamic and engaging qualities, interactive content fits as a promising technique for teaching educators complex artificial intelligence materials. This paper aims to identify the methods course providers use to enhance learning experiences by analyzing data from learners' interactions with the interactive content included in these courses. The research investigates how various forms of interactive content affect learners' engagement and overall course success by employing learning analytics and interaction data. The conclusion of the analysis provides insightful information for future course design and the use of interactive content in AI education. The study's implications offer guidance on incorporating interactive content into various MOOC-based education programs. This approach better equips teachers with the AI knowledge needed to navigate the opportunities and challenges posed by advancing technology in digital education platforms.

articleTitle: Solving Vehicle Routing Problem with Considering Traffic Congestion Using Tabu Search Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICELTICs)
abstract: The increasing population in urban areas has resulted in increasing challenges faced by large cities in the world to design effective and efficient transportation systems, both for people and goods. The increasingly severe traffic conditions in urban areas make the situation even more difficult. As the number of vehicles of various types increases, the level of congestion increases rapidly. This shows the importance of considering traffic congestion in designing logistics systems in urban areas. Although there are many studies on vehicle routing problems (VRP), those that consider congestion are still limited. This study aims to solve a VRP by considering traffic congestion using a heuristic method based on the Tabu Search algorithm. Tabu Search (TS) is a type of metaheuristic. The success of TS is due to its ability to direct the search process so as not to get trapped in the local optimum, in large part, like many other metaheuristics. It has been widely used to solve complex combinatorial optimization problems. The performance of the solution resulted from this study shows that compared to the commercial solver, the heuristic can solve the VRP with a gap of 0.00%. It means that the proposed heuristic can result in optimal solutions for small data. For large data, the performance of the proposed heuristic is compared to the previous study. Compared to the previous study, the heuristic results in a better solution with 5% of improvement.

articleTitle: Emotion Classification for the 2024 General Election Using Lexicon Approach and Deep Learning Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICELTICs)
abstract: The 2024 general election in Indonesia has been a major highlight in the development of democracy, triggering diverse emotional reactions amongst society. Various emotions such as anger, anticipation, disgust, fear, joy, sadness, surprise, and trust appeared on various social media platforms, especially X platform. This research uses datasets obtained using crawling techniques on the X platform. The method used is the NRC Lexicon approach to label emotions by mapping words that contain emotions in the text. Anger emotion is the most dominant emotion with a percentage reaching 33.36%. This research involves the use of deep learning models, namely Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), to classify emotions from the analyzed texts. In addition, this research also explores the application of the SMOTE technique to handle class imbalance in the data. With the application of SMOTE to the RNN model, the accuracy achieved was 74.47%, and in the LSTM model with the application of SMOTE, the accuracy reached 90.49%. The LSTM model (without SMOTE) achieved an accuracy value of 98.52%, precision 90.48% recall 87.48%, and f1-score 87.48%. While the RNN model (without SMOTE) achieved 92.52% accuracy, 90.48% precision, 85.75% recall, and 87.48% f1-score. The comparison with the RNN model confirms the superiority of LSTM in overcoming complexity and long-term patterns in structured text data.

articleTitle: A Taxonomy of Banking Financial Model in Study of Computer Science
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICELTICs)
abstract: In the dynamic aspect of banking, the ability to bank financial models accurately is paramount for strategic decision-making, risk management, and regulatory compliance. A robust financial model serves as a cornerstone for understanding the complexities of banking operations, assessing profitability, and optimizing resource allocation. However, despite the extensive research in this field, there remains a notable gap in the literature regarding certain aspects of banking financial models, especially the utilization of computer science in the field. Therefore, this paper proposes a taxonomy of the banking financial model in computer science studies. We utilized a taxonomy approach introduced by Nickerson et al. [1] with the conceptual-to-empirical (C2E) technique to construct our taxonomy for organizing and categorizing computer science fields into hierarchical groups based on shared similar objects and characteristics. Based on the result, our taxonomy advised structuring and describing banking financial models through five objects, thirteen dimensions, and 127 characteristics in which the risk assessment algorithm, data encryption, optimization algorithm, and Monte Carlo simulation are dimensions discussed more often. Furthermore, the empirical examination allows researchers to identify the utilization of integrating an optimal decision support system with uncertainty handling and software architecture in this research domain as a potential future work.

articleTitle: Optimizing Pomegranate Growth Stage Detection Using YOLOv8 and Hybrid Machine Learning Approaches
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICELTICs)
abstract: Pomegranates, valued for their nutritional and antioxidant properties, require precise growth stage monitoring to optimize yield and quality. This study aims to detect pomegranate growth stages using the YOLOv8 deep learning model integrated with hybrid machine learning techniques. A dataset of 5857 images depicting five stages of pomegranate growth, including Bud, Flower, Early-Fruit, Mid-Growth, and Ripe, was pre- processed with Region of Interest (ROI) extraction, resizing, and normalization. The YOLOv8 model was fine-tuned to serve as a direct classifier and a feature extractor. Extracted features were refined using the Random Forest (RF) model and classified with Logistic Regression (LR), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGB). Ensemble methods such as stacking and voting further enhanced classification accuracy. Results showed significant improvements in performance metrics, with the hybrid approach outperforming the individual YOLOv8 model. F1 Score values for YOLOv8, LR, SVM, XGB, Stacking, and Voting were 90.0%, 93.1%, 93.4%, 93.8%, 94.7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>, and 95.0%, respectively. The voting technique achieved the highest F1-Score, showing a 5% improvement, demonstrating that combining YOLOv8 with machine learning models enhances accuracy and robustness. This research provides a scalable solution for agricultural monitoring, offering valuable insights into integrating deep learning and machine learning for effective crop management.

articleTitle: DrivEye: A Computer Vision-Based Object Detection System to Measure the Distance Between Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICELTICs)
abstract: Traffic accidents are a serious problem worldwide, resulting in thousands of lives lost and millions injured every year. One of the greatest causes of accidents is driver negligence in maintaining a safe distance between vehicles. This research was performed to develop an advanced driver assistance system (ADAS) system capable of real-time measurement of the distances between vehicles and objects or from vehicles in front on a mobile application that can provide warnings when such distances become too small. This system is a simplified version of expensive sensors or lidars, which are difficult to integrate into vehicles. The system uses the YOLOv5 model to detect and identify vehicles using a smartphone camera. The YOLOv5 model training resulted in a mean average precision (mAP) value of 90%, indicating high object detection capability. The system was integrated into a mobile application to enable real-time vehicle detection. Tests showed that the system could detect and identify vehicles as well as predict the distance between vehicles with an accuracy of 94.08%. This research showed that the system can replace both sensors and lidar for measuring the distances to objects in front of a vehicle in real-time using only a smartphone.

articleTitle: The Efficient Development of Conflict Structure Datasets for Evaluating Sentiment Recognition Bias in Large Language Models
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICELTICs)
abstract: The rapid advancement of AI technology has led to the development of large language models (LLMs) that acquire extensive general knowledge from vast amounts of text data and are utilized in various tasks. However, LLMs also inherit biases from their training data, resulting in discriminatory behavior related to gender, race, and political ideologies. In the field of national security, sentiment recognition bias towards specific countries poses significant problems. Previous studies have developed datasets to evaluate these biases, but several issues remain in their methods. This study proposes a new method for developing datasets to evaluate sentiment recognition bias in LLMs, using tweet data related to the Ukraine-Russia war. The method involves automated sentiment labeling and anonymization using LLMs to create efficient and high-precision datasets. GPT -3.5-turbo was used for initial sentiment labeling, with human corrections applied to select tweets positive towards Ukraine and negative towards Russia. Anonymization processing with LLMs ensured specific names did not influence bias evaluation. Experimental results confirmed the proposed method effectively evaluates sentiment recognition bias in LLMs across various conflict structures. Metrics such as Emotion Inversion Consistency Rate (EICR), Positive Odds, and Negative Odds quantitatively assessed biases. The results clearly demonstrated LLMs‘ emotional biases towards specific countries and their recognition of conflict structures. In conclusion, this study presents a new method for evaluating biases in LLMs and demonstrates its effectiveness. Future research will focus on expanding dataset size and improving anonymization to further enhance fairness and reliability. This study lays the groundwork for more robust evaluations of LLM biases.‘’

articleTitle: Enhanced Prediction of Atopic Dermatitis Severity Using Advanced Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICELTICs)
abstract: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronic inflammatory skin condition with increasing prevalence in Indonesia, presenting significant challenges in diagnosis and management. This study introduces a novel approach to objectively classify AD severity using advanced machine learning techniques and comprehensive color feature extraction from clinical images. A unique dataset of 3,037 high-resolution photographs from 250 Acehnese patients was collected at RSUD Dr. Zainoel Abidin, captured using a standardized 12-megapixel smartphone protocol. Ninety color features were extracted from multiple color spaces to capture the diverse visual characteristics of AD lesions. Four state-of-the-art machine learning models - XGBoost, CatBoost, LightGBM, and Random Forest - were employed to classify AD severity into four categories: None, Mild, Moderate, and Severe. Models were trained and evaluated using various performance metrics including accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. Results showed high performance across all models, with LightGBM achieving the highest accuracy of 95.07%, followed closely by XGBoost at 94.74%. SHAP analysis revealed that standard deviation features, particularly those related to hue and chrominance variability across different color spaces, were most influential in severity classification. This research demonstrates the potential of combining advanced color feature extraction with machine learning to create an objective, consistent, and accessible tool for AD severity assessment. The findings have significant implications for improving AD management in resource-limited settings and standardizing severity assessment in clinical practice and research

articleTitle: Developing a Classification Model for Early Stage Alzheimer's Detection Using MRI Images with Deep Learning Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICELTICs)
abstract: Alzheimer's disease, a neurodegenerative disorder caused by the deterioration of brain neurons, results in a decline in daily functional abilities and remains incurable. However, medication can slow its progression, making early detection critical for prevention. This study aims to develop a classification model for early-stage Alzheimer's detection. The dataset utilized is the “Modified Alzheimer's Dataset,” comprising 6,400 axial view MRI brain images categorized into four classes: Non-Demented (3,200 images), Very Mild Demented (2,240 images), Mild Demented (896 images), and Moderate Demented (64 images). The training process employed pretrained models, SqueezeNet and EfficientNet. To address class imbalance, preprocessing was performed using the SMOTE-ENN technique. Post-preprocessing, various hyperparameter configurations were tested on both models. The best configurations for each archi-tecture were then analyzed to compare their performance. The highest accuracies achieved by the optimal models of SqueezeNet and EfficientNet were 98.75% and 99.25%, respectively.

articleTitle: Ontology for Intelligent Disease Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICELTICs)
abstract: This research develops a comprehensive ontology to improve intelligent disease diagnosis by addressing gaps in current medical ontologies. By systematically organizing and analyzing medical data, the ontology enhances diagnostic accuracy and efficiency. The methodology includes a literature study and the development of an ontology-based on key concepts and relationships in the health domain. Results indicate that a more complete ontology supports better clinical decisions. Despite challenges in data collection and validation, the study contributes to improved medical care quality. Future research should focus on integrating machine learning and AI to enhance reasoning and prediction capabilities

articleTitle: Forecasting Stocks Prices with GRU and Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICELTICs)
abstract: Stocks represent a type of investment, reflecting ownership of a company. However, investing in stocks carries risks due to the potential for changes in share values. AI has gained significant traction in the financial sector, particularly in stock markets. To reduce mistakes in investing in shares, you can use Artificial Intelligence (AI). This capability has proven invaluable in forecasting stock prices, but the main challenge lies in minimizing the error rate of the algorithms used. Additionally, there is a demand for lightweight machine-learning architectures capable of fast and efficient processing. This research aims to overcome this problem by utilizing the GRU algorithm and the attention gate mechanism to design an architecture that is lighter than existing research while increasing the performance of the forecasting stocks value. The results of the proposed model provide better results when compared to previously existing architectures, where the proposed model obtains RSME results of 0.0243.

articleTitle: Onboarding Employees in the Metaverse: The HR Perspective
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICELTICs)
abstract: Creating a virtual environment in which people worldwide can access and live is central to the metaverse concept. The COVID-19 crisis expedited the development of this technology. Metaverse is now being seen as an answer to the problem that was created during the pandemic when there was a need to connect while keeping the social norms of physical distancing. Organizations seem to be grappling with the absence of face-to-face interaction that is necessary for working and cultivating team dynamics and see the metaverse as a tool that can fill this gap. However, the technology is still in its nascent stage, and like every technology, it has its shortcomings. In this paper, we have used both primary and secondary resources to understand the impact of the metaverse on organizations, especially the HR functions, where the interaction happens the most, right from the start of the interview to induction to the final onboarding of employees. Through semi-structured interviews, we ought to find out the perspective of HR Managers using these technologies in their company for such HR processes. Also using secondary data sources like research papers and articles published in reputed journals and magazines we intend to understand the extent to which this technology is being discussed in public and the future research agenda.

articleTitle: Optimizing Broiler Chicken Supply Chains Under Uncertain Average Growth Rate Acceleration
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICELTICs)
abstract: Effective planning of the broiler chicken production chain heavily relies on a comprehensive understanding of the factors influencing growth and final carcass weight. The broiler chicken supply chain includes various stages, from breeders to retailers. This study analyzes the impact of growth uncertainty in broiler chickens by considering aspects of maintenance management, feed consumption, mortality rates, productivity, and market demand scenarios. The research method uses a two-stage stochastic program and Mixed Integer Linear Programming (MILP) to optimize lot-sizing and lot-allocation in the broiler chicken supply chain planning. MILP is applied to maximize the efficiency and responsiveness of lot-sizing and lot-allocation to market demand. Two-stage stochastic modeling allows for the separation of long-term and short-term decisions, enabling adjustments based on uncertain conditions. By simulating various production scenarios, potential issues and improvement opportunities within the supply chain can be identified. Production data is analyzed to ensure that the size and weight of broiler chickens meet market specifications and demands, thereby enhancing customer satisfaction and operational efficiency. The implementation of an integrated broiler chicken supply chain is believed to improve production and distribution efficiency, enabling the fulfillment of market demand at optimal costs. By ensuring this alignment, the research contributes to increased customer satisfaction and operational efficiency. Meeting market specifications not only improves product quality but also strengthens the company's competitive position in the market. Higher operational efficiency is also achieved through more effective reductions in production and distribution costs.

articleTitle: Machine Learning for Antiviral Drug Discovery: Application of XGBoost-TPE for Predicting Bioactivity of Hepatitis C Inhibitors
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICELTICs)
abstract: The development of effective antiviral medications remains a priority, particularly in combating diseases caused by viral infections such as the Hepatitis C virus (HCV). Despite the success of direct-acting antivirals, challenges such as drug-resistant strains and high treatment costs necessitate ongoing efforts to discover novel antiviral agents. Traditional drug discovery methods are laborious, costly, and resource-intensive, highlighting the need for more efficient approaches. Machine learning (ML) offers a promising alternative, with Quantitative Structure-Activity Relationship (QSAR) modeling widely used to predict the bioactivity of new compounds based on their chemical properties. However, the performance of ML models like Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) depends on complex hyperparameter optimization. This study demonstrates that combining XGBoost with the Tree-structured Parzen Estimator (TPE) significantly enhances the performance and efficiency of predicting the bioactivity of HCV NS3 inhibitors. The XGBoost-TPE model achieved superior performance with an R-squared of 0.856, root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.640, and mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.452, outperforming baseline models such as Support Vector Regression and standard XGBoost. The study highlights the potential of combining XGBoost with TPE to enhance the efficiency and accuracy of antiviral drug discovery, providing a scalable methodology for screening large libraries of chemical compounds and contributing to developing more effective antiviral therapies.

articleTitle: The Influence of TikTok as a Marketing Tool for MSMEs on Public Buyer Interest
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICELTICs)
abstract: Humans develop technology as an extension to overcome their limitations in conquering space and time. In the era of globalization, the increasingly rapid development of information technology cannot be avoided. The development of technology and information has changed society's culture, lifestyle, and means of communication. In particular, the Internet is very useful for gathering and sharing information rapidly and using less resources. An example of sharing information is through social media called TikTok, a program launched by ByteDance Inc. In 2016, it became a global phenomenon and an effective marketing tool for micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs). TikTok allows engaging video content to promote its products and reach a wider audience through creative content. This research uses a quantitative approach and questionnaire to analyze the impact of TikTok on consumers' buying interest. The research shows that TikTok significantly increases brand awareness, brand image, and consumer purchasing interest. Using TikTok as a marketing tool makes it possible to compete more effectively in the digital market. Data collected from 200 respondents in Jakarta shows that TikTok has a positive impact on consumer purchasing decisions through the variables of brand awareness, brand image, and behavior. These results provide valuable insights for MSMEs to develop more effective digital marketing strategies.

articleTitle: A Spatial Approach to Analyze the Distribution and Risk Factors of Stunting in North Sumatra With the K-Means Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICELTICs)
abstract: This research aims to analyze the spatial pattern of stunting incidents in North Sumatra based on family economic factors using the K-Means algorithm. The data used includes the incidence of stunting, family economics, and spatial data (geographical coordinates) from the Central Statistics Agency (BPS) and Basic Health Research (Riskesdas). The elbow and silhouette analysis methods determine the optimal number of clusters, resulting in four clusters: Cluster 1 with varying economic conditions but very limited access to health and sanitation and a high incidence of stunting; Cluster 2 with low economic conditions, limited access to health, and a high incidence of stunting; Cluster 3 with medium economic conditions and moderate stunting incidence; Cluster 4 with good economic conditions and health services and a low incidence of stunting. Validation using the Silhouette Coefficient shows an average value of 0.553, indicating good clustering quality. The analysis shows that family economic factors, access to health services, and sanitation conditions have a significant effect on the incidence of stunting. Policy and intervention recommendations are focused on clusters 1 and 2 with interventions including increasing access and quality of nutrition, health services, improving sanitation, economic empowerment, and health education and counseling.

articleTitle: Leveraging Advanced Vision-Language Model in Medical Visual Question Answering
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICELTICs)
abstract: Visual Question Answering (VQA) in healthcare represents a groundbreaking method that utilizes sophisticated computational tools to interpret intricate details within medical images. These images often involve intricate question variations and high degrees of abstraction, posing significant challenges for traditional analysis methods. This study examines the BLIP model, which integrates Vision Transformers (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V$</tex>iT) for robust image encoding with transformers for nuanced text encoding, aiming to address these challenges effectively. Our comprehensive evaluation on the Path Vqa dataset shows the model's accuracy at 83.91%, including 97.43% for close-ended questions and 66.15% for open-ended questions. Similarly, on the VQA-RAD dataset, the model achieves an overall accuracy of 82.86%, with 87.85% for close-ended questions and 76.82% for open-ended questions. These results demonstrate the BLIP model's adeptness at managing different types of questions, highlighting its potential to significantly enhance diagnostic processes and decision-making in medical VQA applications, this renders it an essential resource in clinical environments and medical investigations.

articleTitle: Implementation of Virtual Try-On for Clothing Products Using Deep Learning Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICELTICs)
abstract: Virtual Try-On technology has emerged as a break-through innovation in the e-commerce industry, allowing consumers to virtually try on clothing products before making a purchase. Deep learning methods, such as Generative Ad-versarial Networks (GANs), generate accurate simulations of how a garment will appear on the user's body. This technology addresses key challenges, such as uncertainties in clothing sizes and fits, which often hinder the online shopping experience. The development of virtual try-on continues to advance rapidly, enabling users to test products virtually before committing to a purchase. The outcomes of the virtual try-on model are evaluated based on achieved accuracy and visual results. Accu-racy is measured using Structural Similarity (SSIM) scores and Inception Score (IS). This study is based on previous research [1] that applied this technology to clothing using hyperparameters such as 20 epochs, a learning rate of 0.0002, and a batch size of 8 with a training dataset of 14,221 data. The previous study achieved an SSIM score of 0.845 and an IS score of 2.829. In this study, further development was conducted by testing different hyperparameters on smaller resources. The model with the highest accuracy was trained using hyperparameters of batch size 3, learning rate 0.0002, over 20 epochs, with a dataset of 1,000 training samples. This model achieved an SSIM score of 0.795071 and an IS score of 2.2008. The clothing items effectively covered the model's body during inference. The virtual try-on implementation was executed through a simple web interface using Flask.

articleTitle: Classification of Thalassemia Based on Red Blood Cell Images using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICELTICs)
abstract: The advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) have proven to be highly beneficial across various domains, particularly in the field of image processing. One significant application of AI-driven image processing is in the medical field, where it facilitates early disease detection. Thalassemia, a genetic blood disorder, is one such condition that can be predicted with the assistance of AI. This study employs deep learning techniques to detect Thalassemia based on red blood smear imaging. The images are classified into three classes Thalassemia, Iron Deficiency Anemia (IDA), and Normal Red Blood Cells (RBC) images. Deep learning pretrained network AlexNet and ResNet-50 were utilized for image classification. The experimental results demonstrate that both models perform satisfactorily, with accuracy rates surpassing 95%. ResNet-50 exhibited superior overall performance, achieving an average accuracy of 99.36% ± 1.62%, along with a precision of 98.62% ± 2.86%, sensitivity of 99.74% ± 0.45%, specificity of 98.01% ± 4.44%, and an F-score of 98.49% ± 3.56%. Despite ResNet-50's higher accuracy, AlexNet demonstrated greater efficiency in training time, completing the process in an average of 270 seconds. These findings highlight the potential of deep learning models, particularly ResNet-50, in enhancing the early detection of Thalassemia.
